$comment: Known-failing tests, by name. Generated by `node tools/test-ratchet.mjs --update` -- do not hand-edit the list. Lowering this file is the visible, reviewable act of accepting that a failure was fixed; raising it is the visible act of accepting a new one. Notes are preserved across --update, so keep them.

knownFailures.name: agents generator emits exact canonical control targets for every truthful presence status
knownFailures.note: ENVIRONMENT-COUPLED, and this one genuinely is -- unlike the discovery row below, whose coupling note was false. The fixture calls copyCanonicalReaders, which copied config/agent-org.json out of the LIVE canonical tree (C:/Users/joshp/Desktop/toolsenabled-current, via gen-projection-lib.mjs CANONICAL_ROOT at :26). That file is owner intent and is edited with no commit in THIS repo behind it: R1186/R1187 retired the 'claude' agent id, so declaredAgent() threw 'missing declared fixture agent claude'. Verified the generator side is CORRECT, not buggy -- gen-agents.mjs builds declared straight from org.agents with no filtering. Two fixes now exist and only one should survive: 5e6eca5 re-syncs the fixture to today's org (keeps the coupling; expect this row to return on the next reorg), efa2104 makes the fixture write its own org (removes it). If 5e6eca5 alone is kept, this note should stay and name config/agent-org.json as the trigger.

knownFailures.name: browser reader accepts all checked-in available projections
knownFailures.note: TEST is wrong, code is right. Commit 060506c (T4c) deliberately replaced all seven shipped projections with unavailable envelopes to get the owner's private snapshot out of the installer; this test's loop asserts result.ok === true for EVERY checked-in payload, so it now asserts a policy that was intentionally reversed. Its own name says 'available projections' but the body never filters for them. THE TRAP FOR WHOEVER FIXES IT: relaxing the loop to tolerate ok:false silently DELETES the reader's accept-path coverage, because after T4c no shipped payload can exercise ok:true, and nothing else covers it -- projection-contract.test.mjs:59 covers only the unavailable path, and tools/test/empty-envelopes.test.mjs already asserts the shipped-envelope policy in full (exact keys, ok:false, data:null, sources:[], plus the owner-data scan), so re-asserting that here adds nothing. The honest shape is: assert the reader reports each shipped payload EXACTLY as shipped (result.ok === (payload.ok !== false), result.data deep-equals payload, and on unavailable that result.reason is the envelope's OWN reason, never one the reader invented), AND keep a constructed available payload so the accept path still runs. Guard the loop against vacuity too -- count the domains it actually visited.

knownFailures.name: contract #7: a real listen error that is not "address in use" propagates unchanged
knownFailures.note: ADJUDICATED: the TEST is wrong, the code is right. Do not 'fix' shell/port-scan.cjs to make this pass. Ruling with full evidence at C:/Users/joshp/Desktop/toolsenabled-current/reports/lanes/portscan-adjudication.md, cited by commit ab07f25. RETRYABLE_LISTEN_ERRORS at shell/port-scan.cjs:11 includes EACCES deliberately: on Windows, EACCES from a plain listen() on an unprivileged port is in practice an OS per-port exclusion (Hyper-V/WinNAT reserved range, confirmed on this host via `netsh interface ipv4 show excludedportrange protocol=tcp`), which is mechanically equivalent to EADDRINUSE, so advancing to the next candidate is correct -- giving up strands the user. The original error is not destroyed either; it survives at error.cause, just not at the top-level error.code this clause asserts on. Clause 7 picked EACCES as its 'must propagate raw' exemplar, which is backwards for Windows. The test-side reformulation is owned by a separate lane. ALSO NOTE, so a green reading elsewhere is not misread: listExcludedTcpPorts() SKIPS the whole case on a host with no OS-excluded TCP port, so a clean CI box skips rather than passes -- green there would not prove anything was fixed.

knownFailures.name: discovery walks 4610-4619 in order and authenticates only after an exact valid tuple
knownFailures.note: CORRECTED 2026-08-08. The previous note here said this test was ENVIRONMENT-COUPLED to a live listener on 4610 (pid 9428) and told the reader to confirm bridge state before lowering. THAT WAS FALSE and it was written by the coordinator, who has confirmed the error. This test opens NO sockets: tools/test/mission-bridge.test.mjs replaces globalThis.fetch wholesale, so the walk is entirely against a stub. The file that does use real sockets is tools/test/shell-port-scan.test.mjs, on 4601-4609; the two were conflated. Measured three ways: (1) with no window.mcShell the call returns code BRIDGE_BOOTSTRAP_PROOF_UNAVAILABLE after visiting only 4610/4611/4612 through the stub; (2) adding ONLY a valid mcShell.getBridgeProof makes it green with every original assertion intact; (3) with every stubbed fetch rejecting, exactly 10 calls occur and the result is BRIDGE_DISCOVERY_UNAVAILABLE. A real listener is present on 4610 (pid 32088 at time of writing, not 9428 -- the old note's pid was stale too) and is never reached. THE REAL CAUSE was a stale fixture: shell/bridge-proof.cjs added a bootstrap proof requirement, and this test predated it. Fixed in 50dfeb7. Left in this file only because --update was not safe to run while other lanes were mid-flight; re-run `node tools/test-ratchet.mjs --update` to drop this row. THE LESSON WORTH KEEPING: a false explanation attached to a real failure is worse than no explanation, because it forecloses the investigation.

knownFailures.name: research view distinguishes unavailable observations from observed-empty data
knownFailures.note: TEST is wrong, code is right. Same cause as the browser-reader row: commit 060506c (T4c) made public/data/research.json an unavailable envelope with data:null, so `envelope.data.findingsRegister` throws TypeError 'Cannot read properties of null'. The VIEW half of this test (the regexes over src/views/research.js) still passes; only the half asserting the SHIPPED FILE'S CONTENT is dead, and that half was asserting a file that policy now requires to be empty. SEARCH BEFORE REBUILDING: tools/test/research-generator.test.mjs already proves every content fact here deterministically against a temp fixture -- findingsRegister.value deep-equals [], failureTaxonomy.ok false, openQuestions.ok false, 7 safe / 7 flagged, flagged carry authorizationReason and no summary, byte-idempotent, sentinel absent. The only clauses it does NOT yet carry are methodNotes.value.length === 7 and the exact reason string 'source-out-of-scope'; move those there rather than inventing new coverage. Keep the view assertions where they are.

knownFailures.note: TEST is wrong, code is right. Identical cause to the row above -- `envelope.data.corpusCatalog` throws on data:null after commit 060506c (T4c). Its view assertions (lockedReportMarkup carries report?.title and report?.authorizationReason and NOT summary/path/bytes/dateObserved/source/id) pass and are the part actually worth keeping; the 7-safe/7-locked counts read the shipped file and are already proven against a fixture in tools/test/research-generator.test.mjs.
